author: tcoratger
content:
Hmm, it’s difficult to interpret the benchmark based on the numbers alone, but here is my take: hyperthreading doesn't help here because it only helps when a thread is frequently waiting—for instance, while waiting for data to arrive from memory. During such intervals, the other thread can utilize the units that are free.

In our case, however, that doesn't apply, so we gain nothing from it. The process almost never waits; it essentially performs a continuous sequence of vectorized multiplications without any pauses, while reading from memory at maximum bandwidth. Since the core is already 100% occupied, there is nothing left for a second thread to take advantage of.
